title: Set a file's timestamp to a specific date and time
summary: Use touch with the -t option to change a file's modification time to a specific date and time. This is useful for organizing files or testing scripts that depend on file dates.

steps.explain: Use the -t option followed by the date in YYYYMMDDHHMM.SS format. Add -c to prevent creating the file if it doesn't exist.

placeholders.name: DATE
placeholders.description: Date and time in YYYYMMDDHHMM.SS format

alternatives.explain: Use the -d option to set the timestamp by parsing a human-readable string like 'last year' or '5 hours ago'.
Use the setfile command with the -m flag to set the modification date. Replace <DATE_TIME> with the desired date in MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS format and <FILE_PATH> with the path to the file.

placeholders.name: DATE_TIME
placeholders.description: The new modification date and time in MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS format

placeholders.name: FILE_PATH
placeholders.description: Path to the file(s) to modify
